testCases.title: Complete the meditation breathing exercise accessibly
testCases.description: Validate the primary meditation breathing experience end to end: configure one-second inhale, hold, and exhale phases for two cycles; verify start, phase countdown and cycle progress; pause and resume without advancing; reset and restart; complete the exercise; verify concise aria-live phase/completion announcements; reload to confirm preferences persist while session state resets; and confirm reduced-motion behavior.

steps.label: Set up and execute the complete stateful timer workflow using browser clock control so phase, pause, reset, cycle, completion, and local preference behavior are deterministic.
steps.gherkinStep: Given the complete meditation breathing exercise happy path is exercised deterministically

steps.label: Verify semantic controls, live-region announcement cadence, keyboard operation, visible focus, and reduced-motion behavior.
steps.gherkinStep: Then the meditation breathing experience is accessible and honors reduced motion

executable.selector: Complete the meditation breathing exercise accessibly

customStepJustifications.missingCapability: Deterministic browser-clock control across a multi-phase timer plus reload-localStorage assertions
customStepJustifications.whyLocatorsAndExistingStepsAreInsufficie: The registry exposes atomic click, fill, and text assertions but no reusable navigation, clock advancement, reload, localStorage corruption/recovery, or multi-phase timer state capability. Atomic waits would make baseline and implementation validation slow and flaky.

customStepJustifications.missingCapability: Accessibility semantics, live-region cadence, focus visibility, and reduced-motion media emulation
customStepJustifications.whyLocatorsAndExistingStepsAreInsufficie: The available generic steps cannot inspect ARIA live-region behavior over timer transitions, emulate prefers-reduced-motion, or assert focus-visible styling. These require Playwright-level browser assertions.
